parts.problem_md: What is the purpose of a cheque counterfoil?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- When a cheque is written, some basic details are also filled in on the cheque counterfoil
- These details can then be used to record the details of the cheque payment in the cash book

**A** is incorrect; a paying-in slip** **is used when depositing cash and/or cheques into a bank account

**B** is incorrect; the cheque itself (backed up by funds in the bank account) is used to pay for goods purchased by cheque

**D** is incorrect; the cheque counterfoil is filled in and kept by the person writing a cheque, so it will not generally be available to a person who has received the cheque

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: It is used to pay a cheque into the bank account.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: It is used to pay for goods purchased by cheque.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: It is used to record a cheque payment in the cash book.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: It is used to record a cheque received in the cash book.

parts.problem_md: Which one of the following documents does a trader issue to a credit customer to remind the customer that a payment is due?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is D**

- A statement of account is issued by a supplier, and shows all transactions between a credit customer and the supplier within a given time frame
- If the customer still owes money to the supplier, this amount will appear on the statement of account

**A** is incorrect; a supplier issues a credit note to a credit customer when the balance on an invoice is reduced

**B** is incorrect; a credit customer issues a debit note to a supplier to request a reduction in the balance of an invoice

**C** is incorrect; a receipt is used as a record of a cash payment, and is issued by a supplier to a customer when the customer pays for goods using cash

parts.problem_md: Which one of the following documents is provided by a supplier and reduces the amount owed by a customer?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- A supplier issues a credit note to a credit customer when the balance due on an invoice is reduced

  - For example because goods have been returned, or the customer has been overcharged
- A credit customer may *request* a reduction by issuing a debit note to the supplier

  - But the reduction is not actually made until the supplier issues a credit note

**B** is incorrect; a credit customer issues a debit note to a supplier to request a reduction in the balance of an invoice

**C** is incorrect; an invoice is a record issued by a supplier to a credit customer when the customer makes a credit purchase

**D** is incorrect; a statement of account is used to show all transactions between a credit customer and a supplier within a given time frame and the balance on the account can increase or decrease

parts.problem_md:
Ben sold goods to Abigail on credit, but some of the goods were damaged in transit.

Which one of the following documents would Abigail send to Ben?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- A credit customer issues a debit note to a supplier to request a reduction in the balance of an invoice

  - For example, if goods are damaged in transit

**A** is incorrect; a supplier issues a credit note to a credit customer when the balance on an invoice is reduced

**C** is incorrect; an invoice is a record issued by a supplier to a credit customer when the customer makes a credit purchase

**D** is incorrect; a statement of account is issued by the supplier and is used to show all transactions between a credit customer and a supplier within a given time frame

parts.problem_md: If a credit customer has returned goods or been overcharged, which one of the following documents would a supplier issue to the customer?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- A supplier issues a credit note to a credit customer when the balance on an invoice is reduced

  - For example because goods have been returned, or the customer has been overcharged

**A** is incorrect; although a cheque may later be sent to the customer if their account has a credit balance and they request to settle up the account

**C** is incorrect; a credit customer issues a debit note to a supplier to request a reduction in the balance of an invoice

**D** is incorrect; an invoice is a record issued by a supplier to a credit customer when the customer makes a credit purchase

parts.problem_md:
Azar purchased goods from Lara.  Azar paid for the goods by bank transfer when he received a statement of account, but Lara says that she has not received the payment.

Which one of the following documents would help Azar check that he had made the payment?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- The amounts of any bank transfers (both sent and received) will appear on the bank statement that Azar receives from the bank

**B** is incorrect; Azar did not pay by cheque, so there will be no cheque counterfoil

**C** is incorrect; a paying-in slip is a document used when depositing cash and/or cheques into a bank account

**D** is incorrect; a petty cash voucher is used to record the transaction when money is taken from a business's petty cash account

parts.problem_md:
In October, Eira sent Gwilym invoices for \$205, \$120 and \$170, and a credit note for \$72. Also in October, Gwilym sent Eira a cheque for \$198 and a debit note for \$80. There was no opening balance on Eira's account at the start of October.

What was the balance on Eira's account in Gwilym's books on 1 November?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- The invoices sent by Eira to Gwilym are all amounts that Gwilym owes to Eira

  - \$205 + \$120 + \$170 = \$495
- The amount owed will be reduced by two things

  - the credit note sent by Eira to Gwilym (which is issued by a supplier to a customer when an invoice is reduced)
  - the cheque sent by Gwilym to Eira (which is a payment by Gwilym against amounts owed to Eira)
  - \$72 + \$198 = \$270
- The debit note sent by Gwilym to Eira does not change the amount owed

  - A credit customer issues a debit note to a supplier to *request* a reduction in the balance of an invoice
  - But no reduction is actually made until the supplier issues a credit note confirming any reduction
- So at the start of November, the amount owed to Eira by Gwilym is

  - \$495 - \$270 = \$225
- An amount owed to Eira is a liability for Gwilym's business

  - So this balance will appear as a credit on Eira's account in Gwilym's books on 1 November

**A** and **B** are incorrect; \$145 is the amount owed by Gwilym to Eira that you would get if you also subtracted the amount of the debit note (\$80) from the invoices

**D** is incorrect; the amount (\$225) is correct, but an amount owed by Gwilym to Eira should be a credit in Eira's account in Gwilym's books, not a debit

parts.problem_md:
Mitig sold goods with a list price of \$70 each.

The terms were as follows

- trade discount when more than 50 items are purchased: 10%
- cash discount if customer pays within 28 days: 6%

How much did Mitig receive in full settlement from a customer who bought 60 items and paid after 30 days?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- The customer bought enough items to qualify for the trade discount, but did not pay quickly enough to qualify for the cash discount

  - So only the 10% trade discount will be applied
- Find the total list price of the goods (60 items at \$70 each)

  - 60 ✕ \$70 = \$4200
- Find the trade discount amount (10% of the total)

  - 10% ✕ \$4200 = \$420
- Subtract the discount from the list price

  - \$4200 - \$420 = \$3780

**A** is incorrect; this is what you would get if you applied the trade discount to a sale of only 50 items

**B** is incorrect; this is what you would get if you applied both discounts (trade and cash) to the total

**D** is incorrect; this is what you would get if you used the cash discount instead of the trade discount

parts.problem_md:
On 1 November, Inaya purchases goods on credit.  The list price of the goods is \$500.  She is given a trade discount of \$50, and if payment is made within 30 days a cash discount of \$20 will be given.

Which amount is credited to the supplier's account on 1 November?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- A trade discount is a reduction in the selling price of goods or services, and is applied before a transaction takes place

  - Therefore on 1 November the amount credited will be the list price minus the trade discount
  - \$500 - \$50 = \$450
- If Inaya pays by the cash discount deadline, then the discount will be recorded at that time in the cash book as a separate entry

  - A cash discount is  not recorded on the same date as part of the same entry for the original credit purchase

**A** is incorrect; this is what you would get if you subtracted the trade and cash discounts from the list price

**C** is incorrect; this is what you would get if you subtracted the cash discount (instead of the trade discount) from the list price

**D** is incorrect; this is simply the list price, without any discount applied

parts.problem_md:
Leandu maintains a full set of accounting records for her business.

Why would it be useful for Leandu to complete the cheque counterfoil when she pays a credit supplier by cheque?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is D**

- The cash book is a book of prime entry, and is the ledger account for the cash and bank accounts

  - All payments made from the bank account should be recorded in the cash book
  - The cheque counterfoil provides a useful record if the amount is not entered into the cash book at the same time as the cheque is written

**A** is incorrect; the purchases account will be updated from the cash book, not directly from entries on cheque counterfoils

**B** is incorrect; the bank reconciliation statement is prepared using entries from the cash book and bank statement, not directly from entries on cheque counterfoils

**C** is incorrect; a cheque counterfoil completed by the person writing a cheque will not normally be accepted as proof of the amount paid

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: It allows her to keep the purchases account up to date.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: It is helpful for preparing the bank reconciliation statement.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: It provides proof of the amount she has paid to the supplier.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: It records information to help her maintain the cash book.

parts.problem_md: Which items are **not** shown on a statement of account?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- Statements of account will always include the statement date, opening and closing balances, and details of any credit notes issued
- They do not show any bank charges

  - A statement of account details transactions between a customer and a supplier
  - Bank charges are a transaction between a customer and a bank, and will appear on a bank statement

**B**, **C** and **D** are incorrect; these are all items that *do* appear on a statement of account
